i1.title: Battery, raw materials, recycling
points: Typical batteries hold 40–90 kWh and lose about 12 % capacity in 300,000 km; warranties run 8–10 years / 150,000–200,000 km (see "Battery & resale").
Switzerland has no raw-material deposits; processing is dominated by China; recycled content stays in the single-digit % until the mid-2040s (BFE/BAFU 2026).

EVs need about 320 Mt of critical-mineral ore, versus more than 100 bn t of fossil fuels extracted in 2024; recycling could cover 10–20 % of lithium/nickel and over 30 % of cobalt demand by 2050 (IEA 2026).

Take-back is free (sestorec, SENS eRecycling, INOBAT); Swiss plants (Batrec, Librec, Kyburz) recover up to 97 % of active materials (company figures); used batteries get a second life as stationary storage.
The EU battery passport applies from 18 Feb 2027; there is no binding Swiss equivalent yet.

i2.title: Front-loaded vs. back-loaded emissions
points: An EV causes most of its emissions in production, a combustion car in operation – driving the old car "to the end" still causes its operating emissions.
A same-size switch saves greenhouse gases in more than 92 % of model combinations (more than 95 % for pure combustion cars).
From about 8,000 km per year switching almost always pays off; below 4,000–5,000 km per year mostly not.
The saving per km does not depend on the current car's mileage (all BFE/INFRAS 2025).

email.subject: Request: agenda item for the next owners' meeting, charging infrastructure
email.body:
Dear [Name of property management],

I own a flat at Musterstrasse 1, 9000 St. Gallen, parking space [number]. I am planning to switch to an electric car and would like to charge it at my parking space.

I therefore ask you to put the following item on the agenda of the next owners' meeting:
"Installation of charging infrastructure at parking space [number] / in the shared garage, including the cost split and the use of the shared electrical installation."

Please also let me know:
1. Which voting quorum applies to this decision in our community, and by when I need to submit the motion?
2. Whether you can obtain offers for the installation in advance, so that the owners can decide on a concrete proposal.

The EnergieSchweiz guide on charging infrastructure in condominiums, with a template motion and a questionnaire in its annex, is available here: https://www.energieschweiz.ch/programme/ladeinfrastruktur/werkzeuge/ladeinfrastruktur-im-stockwerkeigentum/

Thank you for your support.

Kind regards,
[Your name]
[Telephone / email]

subsidies.name: Ladestationen
subsidies.description: Die Stadt St.Gallen fördert die Installation von Ladestationen für Elektrofahrzeuge. Voraussetzung für die Förderung ist, dass die E-Ladestation rund um die Uhr für die öffentliche Nutzung zur Verfügung steht und auf einer öffentlichen Plattform sichtbar ist. Für Elektro-Ladestationen, die Ost-mobil neues Fenster, dem Ostschweizer Netzwerk für E-Mobilität angeschlossen sind,  werden höhere Förderbeiträge ausbezahlt.
subsidies.description_en: The city of St. Gallen funds the installation of charging stations for electric vehicles. The condition for funding is that the e‑charging station is available around the clock for public use and is visible on a public platform. Higher funding contributions are paid for e‑charging stations that are connected to Ost‑mobil's new window, the Eastern Swiss network for e‑mobility.

charging_time.home_ac: With a home wallbox (11 kW AC) one overnight session covers several days of typical use: charge 1-2 times per week overnight.
charging_time.public_ac: At a public AC point the car stays several hours, for example overnight or during work.
charging_time.public_dc: Fast charging (DC) takes about 20-30 minutes for a typical weekly need: charge while shopping.

tips: About 514 sites in Switzerland offer high-power charging (150 kW or more).
The operators with the most high-power points are Energie 360 Grad AG, Tesla, Shell Recharge.
Use a charging card or app that works across several networks (roaming) and check its coverage and prices for these operators before you travel.
info_b.source: BFE ich-tanke-strom (charging points with 150 kW or more)

countries.coverage_statement: Dense public charging (336 points per 100k inhabitants, 30,886 points in total); balanced AC/DC mix (DC share 29%).
countries.general_tips: Dense network with a strong DC share; alpine transit routes (A1/A2/A12) are well covered. Use a roaming card/app (your Swiss charging card or a multi-network app) and check its coverage and roaming prices for the country before travelling. Bring your own Type 2 cable for AC charging; CCS Combo 2 is the DC standard across Europe. Under AFIR (EU/EEA), newer public fast chargers must accept ad-hoc payment by (contactless) card and show the price per kWh before you start. Plan fast-charge stops on long routes; on TEN-T core corridors pools every 60 km with 150+ kW points are guaranteed.

statements.text: Kept for 1 year, Option 1 (M3, new) costs about CHF 18,400 more (does not pay off within 12 years); Option 2 (L3, new) costs about CHF 29,600 more (does not pay off within 12 years) compared with keeping your VW Golf 7 1.0 TSI.

Kept for 2 years, Option 1 (M3, new) costs about CHF 22,300 more (does not pay off within 12 years); Option 2 (L3, new) costs about CHF 37,600 more (does not pay off within 12 years) compared with keeping your VW Golf 7 1.0 TSI.

Kept for 3 years, Option 1 (M3, new) costs about CHF 26,600 more (does not pay off within 12 years); Option 2 (L3, new) costs about CHF 46,000 more (does not pay off within 12 years) compared with keeping your VW Golf 7 1.0 TSI.

Kept for 4 years, Option 1 (M3, new) costs about CHF 30,300 more (does not pay off within 12 years); Option 2 (L3, new) costs about CHF 53,500 more (does not pay off within 12 years) compared with keeping your VW Golf 7 1.0 TSI.

Kept for 5 years, Option 1 (M3, new) costs about CHF 34,400 more (does not pay off within 12 years); Option 2 (L3, new) costs about CHF 61,300 more (does not pay off within 12 years) compared with keeping your VW Golf 7 1.0 TSI.

Kept for 6 years, Option 1 (M3, new) costs about CHF 38,500 more (does not pay off within 12 years); Option 2 (L3, new) costs about CHF 69,000 more (does not pay off within 12 years) compared with keeping your VW Golf 7 1.0 TSI.

Kept for 7 years, Option 1 (M3, new) costs about CHF 38,500 more (does not pay off within 12 years); Option 2 (L3, new) costs about CHF 70,600 more (does not pay off within 12 years) compared with keeping your VW Golf 7 1.0 TSI.

Kept for 8 years, Option 1 (M3, new) costs about CHF 37,700 more (does not pay off within 12 years); Option 2 (L3, new) costs about CHF 71,100 more (does not pay off within 12 years) compared with keeping your VW Golf 7 1.0 TSI.
